title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 198
paragraphs: I think, moreover, that in quality of soil Libya does not greatly surpass Asia or Europe, except for the region of Cinyps—the name being shared with the river. This region is as good as the best of lands for producing Demeter's fruit, and it bears no resemblance at all to the rest of Libya; for it has black soil, is watered by springs, fears no drought, and is not harmed by drinking too much rain—for rain does fall in this part of Libya. The same measures of yield hold here as for the land of Babylon. That land too is good which the Euesperites occupy, for when it bears best it produces a hundredfold; but the region of Cinyps sometimes produces as much as three hundredfold.
